categoryName: Tea, coffee, health drinks, malted beverages

skuLines.examples: Tata Tea Agni, Brooke Bond Taaza, Josh Kadak, Duncans Double Diamond
skuLines.notes: Highest-volume line in the category; support staff, cooks, drivers live on this tier. 18-24 month shelf life means buy 3 months deep despite the hill road. Never OOS.

skuLines.examples: Tata Tea Premium, Red Label, Wagh Bakri Premium Leaf, Society Tea
skuLines.notes: Default household pack for teaching staff and married quarters. Carry at least two brands - tea loyalty is rigid and a substitution refusal sends the wallet to town.

skuLines.examples: Tata Tea Gold, Taj Mahal, Society Premium, Girnar Royal Assam
skuLines.notes: Senior faculty and the 'good tea for guests' occasion. Also the gifting SKU for visitors and donors.

skuLines.line: Loose CTC tea by weight (open bin)
skuLines.examples: Local hill-wholesaler Assam CTC dust, unbranded Marvel/Gemini-type blends
skuLines.seasonality: Winter peak; keep sealed in monsoon
skuLines.notes: Only genuinely high-margin tea line and the classic hill-kirana staple. Buys down the price per cup for the lowest-income staff. Airtight tin, silica, small refills - Sirmaur monsoon humidity cakes loose dust fast.

skuLines.examples: Tata Tea/Girnar 5kg institutional sacks, Wagh Bakri catering pack
skuLines.seasonality: Follows academic session; collapses in vacation
skuLines.marginBand: 10-18% (or internal transfer to the two canteens)
skuLines.notes: ARY supplies its own two canteens plus hostel messes - this is a captive volume, not a retail SKU. Freight per kg drops sharply at 5-10kg, the biggest single logistics win in the category.

skuLines.examples: Goodricke Khaass, Girnar Royal Assam Leaf, Halmari, Teabox Assam
skuLines.notes: Small but real demand from senior faculty and the ~200 international students who drink tea without milk. Loose leaf is 44% of India's tea pack mix, so it is not a niche format nationally.

skuLines.examples: Twinings Origins Darjeeling, Goodricke Thurbo, Makaibari, Golden Tips
skuLines.notes: Buy as gifting/hamper stock, not as everyday tea. Tins survive hill transport and humidity better than paper cartons.

skuLines.examples: Palampur Co-operative Kangra tea, Dharmsala Tea Company, Wah Tea Estate, Manjhee Valley
skuLines.notes: Local-pride line: GI-tagged, grown 5-6 hours away at Palampur, never made as CTC so it is a distinct pale-liquor product. Strongest gift-hamper story ARY has for donors and parents, and short-haul sourcing inside HP.

skuLines.examples: Wagh Bakri Masala Chai, Society Masala Tea, Brooke Bond Taaza Masala Chaska
skuLines.notes: North India runs on masala chai - this is a core line, not a flavour variant. Rs 75 100g pack is the trial and low-income size.

skuLines.examples: Tata Tea Elaichi Chai, Society Elaichi Adrak, Girnar Cardamom
skuLines.notes: Distinct Punjabi/Himachali preference from plain masala; do not treat as interchangeable.

skuLines.line: Tea masala / chai masala spice powder
skuLines.examples: Everest Tea Masala, Catch, MDH, Jalaram with saffron, private-label 50g
skuLines.notes: Cheap, high-margin, tiny cube - almost zero freight cost per rupee of margin. Households that grind their own still buy this in winter.

skuLines.line: Black tea bags - everyday dip tea
skuLines.examples: Tetley Elaichi/Masala bags, Lipton Yellow Label, Taj Mahal dip, Tata Tea Gold bags
skuLines.notes: The hostel-room format: a bag plus a kettle needs no stove, no milk, no pan. Critical for the ~1,500 school and university students and for international students who steep rather than boil. Stock 100-count for value and 25-count for cash-tight weeks.

skuLines.examples: Tetley Ginger, Lipton Masala Chai bags, Organic India ginger-tulsi, Vahdam
skuLines.notes: Sells hardest exactly when Baru Sahib is wettest. Ginger, tulsi, cinnamon, lemon are the four that move.

skuLines.examples: Lipton Clear & Light, Tetley Green, Tea Country Green, Tata Tea Tulsi Green
skuLines.notes: Green tea is a Rs 704 mn/5.7% CAGR Indian market driven by exactly this demographic - health-minded 18-25s and young faculty. 100-count is the value pack a hostel room shares.

skuLines.examples: Lipton Honey Lemon, Tetley Ginger-Mint-Lemon, Tetley Lemon & Honey, Tea Country Lemon-Honey
skuLines.notes: Honey-lemon outsells plain green for first-time drinkers; jasmine and mint round out the set.

skuLines.examples: Lipton Pure & Light 250g, Tetley Long Leaf Green, Kangra green tea
skuLines.notes: Cheaper per cup than bags for heavy drinkers; one facing is enough.

skuLines.examples: Organic India Tulsi Original & Revitalise, Patanjali Divya Peya, Kapiva
skuLines.notes: Herbal tea is India's fastest-growing hot-beverage sub-segment (~12.6% CAGR vs ~3% for tea overall). Benefit-led SKUs - throat, gut, sleep - now sell better than generic 'herbal'.

skuLines.examples: Pukka mint-ginger, chamomile, hibiscus, Blue Tea butterfly pea, lemongrass
skuLines.notes: Also covers the minority of observant residents who avoid caffeine. Chamomile sells to students in exam weeks.

skuLines.examples: Girnar Detox Desi Kahwa, Kashmiri kahwa premix, saffron-almond kahwa
skuLines.notes: A genuinely hill-specific winter drink and an easy sell at 1,000m+ in January. Buy the season's stock in Oct, do not carry it in July.

skuLines.examples: Dabur Ayush Kwath, Baidyanath kadha, Patanjali Giloy Tulsi, Zandu kadha
skuLines.seasonality: Jul-Sep monsoon and Dec-Feb cold season
skuLines.notes: With no chemist 30-50 km away, this is the first thing a hostel warden and a mother reach for at the start of a cold. Stock heavy before monsoon; a stockout here is the kind that costs trust.

skuLines.examples: Girnar Masala/Cardamom Premix Chai, Nestea, Continental premix, Tata Quick Chai
skuLines.notes: Just add hot water - the only tea a hostel room with no stove and no milk can make. Also the refill for any vending machine in departments, hostels or the dispensary, which is the razor-and-blade play for ARY.

skuLines.examples: Wagh Bakri Instant Lemon Tea, Nestea Lemon, Tata Tea Lemon premix
skuLines.notes: The summer half of the tea shelf; small facing, seasonal buy.

skuLines.examples: Nescafe Classic/Sunrise stick packs, Bru sachets, Bevzilla 45-sachet box
skuLines.priceBand: Rs 2-Rs 10 per sachet; Rs 97 per 45-sachet box
skuLines.notes: Sachets are ~40% of India's instant-coffee pack mix and the whole category's entry point. Under a captive-store model these Rs 5-10 units are what let a Rs 1,493/month resident and a hostel student buy coffee at all. Break bulk from boxes and sell loose at the counter.

skuLines.examples: Bru Instant, Nescafe Sunrise, Nescafe Classic
skuLines.notes: Bru is chicory-blended and Sunrise is the value North Indian favourite; both must be on shelf. Jars for quarters, pouches for hostels. Instant coffee keeps 24-36 months - the safest deep-buy in the category.

skuLines.examples: Nescafe Gold, Bru Gold, Colombian Brew, Davidoff
skuLines.notes: Freeze-dried is now ~66% of Indian instant-coffee value and premiumisation is outpacing volume - the trade-up is real, even in tier-3. Two facings: one at Rs ~400-550 and one aspirational.

skuLines.examples: Colombian Brew Hazelnut/Vanilla, Bevzilla flavours, Sleepy Owl Hazelnut
skuLines.notes: Pure 18-25 university play; keep to 2-3 SKUs, they are slow but high-margin.

skuLines.examples: Sunbean Caffe Mix, Bevzilla premix, Cafe Coffee Day premix, Continental
skuLines.notes: Cappuccino/latte/mocha in a sachet with milk powder and sugar built in - solves the no-fresh-milk hostel problem at 11 pm. Same product refills a coffee vending machine.

skuLines.examples: Bru Green Label, Levista Filter, Continental Malgudi, Cothas
skuLines.notes: South India is ~50% of India's coffee market and a residential campus with pan-India faculty and nursing staff always has a filter-coffee minority. One 500g SKU plus one 200g is enough; it stales faster than instant, so buy shallow.

skuLines.examples: Blue Tokai, Sleepy Owl Dark Roast, Third Wave, Continental Xtra R&G
skuLines.notes: One or two SKUs only, aimed at faculty and international students. Sell whole bean only if you can grind to order - stale ground beans kill the line.

skuLines.examples: Nescafe cold coffee mix, Bevzilla cold brew, Amul Kool Cafe powder
skuLines.notes: Nestle pushed cold coffee hard from Apr-2025 and it is now a fixture of the hot-beverage aisle. Seasonal buy only.

skuLines.examples: Sleepy Owl bottled cold coffee, Amul Kool Cafe tetra, Nescafe RTD, Epigamia/Yoga Bar protein cold coffee
skuLines.notes: Impulse at the POS counter and Ary Lite. Needs chiller space; tetra survives the hill road better than glass.

skuLines.examples: Nescafe Decaf, Continental Decaf, Colombian Brew Decaf
skuLines.notes: One facing. Real demand only from older staff advised off caffeine; keep as a special-order line if it does not move in 90 days.

skuLines.examples: Horlicks Classic Malt, Boost, Complan Original
skuLines.seasonality: Winter peak; parents restock at term start and after each visit
skuLines.notes: The classic Indian hostel-parent purchase: parents of Akal Academy boarders buy this for their child's room. Refills are cheaper per gram and repeat - stock both jar and refill, sell the jar once then the refill forever.

skuLines.examples: Cadbury Bournvita, Horlicks Chocolate Delight, Boost, Complan Royale
skuLines.notes: Outsells plain malt with children 5-18, the largest single cohort on campus. Bournvita Zero Added Sugar (Rs 307/500g) now covers the sugar-anxious parent.

skuLines.examples: Bournvita 70g refill, Horlicks 18-25g sachets, Boost sachets
skuLines.notes: How a Rs 1,493/month resident and a support-staff family buy a Rs 460 product at all. A 7.2-bills-per-resident-per-month store lives on these price points; without them the malt category is invisible to half the campus.

skuLines.examples: Junior Horlicks, Pediasure, Nestle Ceregrow, Complan
skuLines.priceBand: Rs 329-345/500g Junior Horlicks; Rs 720/375g and Rs 1,665/950g Pediasure
skuLines.notes: Directly aimed at married staff families with toddlers - a cohort explicitly present here and with nowhere else to buy. Pediasure is a paediatrician-driven purchase: a stockout means a 60-100km round trip. Keep one small and one large size of each.

skuLines.examples: Women's Horlicks (chocolate, caramel), Protinex Mama, Ensure
skuLines.notes: Female teaching and non-teaching staff plus B.Sc Nursing students; calcium/iron claim does the selling.

skuLines.examples: Horlicks Mother's Plus, Protinex Mama, Lactare
skuLines.notes: Small but non-substitutable: a married-quarters campus always has pregnant and nursing women, and this is the hardest item to improvise. One SKU, always in stock.

skuLines.examples: Ensure, Protinex Original/Chocolate, Nutrilite, Fresubin
skuLines.notes: Bought for elderly residents and for recovery/convalescence - the campus dispensary and nursing school create steady pull. Thinnest margins in the category but a trust-building must-stock; 12-18 month shelf life, so buy to demand not to freight.

skuLines.examples: Horlicks Diabetes Plus, Ensure Diabetes Care, Protinex Diabetes Care
skuLines.notes: Malted drinks have split into life-stage SKUs (kids/women/mother/diabetic/elderly) rather than one family jar - the diabetic variant is now a separate must-carry for older staff, not an option.

skuLines.line: Millet / ragi / sattu traditional malt drink
skuLines.examples: Millet Horlicks, ragi malt powder, Bhagirathi/Nutrapoorna chana sattu, Manna health mix
skuLines.notes: The clean-label answer inside a category otherwise dominated by sugar; cheapest health drink per serve, which matters at this ARPU. Low awareness - needs a shelf talker to move.

skuLines.examples: Optimum Nutrition, MuscleBlaze, Fast&Up, Isopure, plant protein
skuLines.notes: Real demand from a 18-25 university cohort with a gym and nowhere to buy. Start with the 5-serve trial packs and one 454g tub only - a Rs 3,000 tub is heavy working capital and counterfeit-sensitive.

skuLines.examples: Boost/Horlicks 180ml tetra, Complan Power Play, Epigamia Turbo, Yoga Bar protein shake
skuLines.notes: Rs 30-40 tetra is a legitimate impulse buy for a school child with pocket money - stock it at Ary Lite and the canteens, not just the main POS. Needs chiller in summer.

skuLines.examples: Cadbury Hot Chocolate, Hershey's, Van Houten, Weikfield
skuLines.notes: A cold hill winter is the single best hot-chocolate market in India. Buy the winter's stock in Sep-Oct; a plain jar sells better than flavoured variants to children.

skuLines.examples: Hershey's Natural Cocoa, Weikfield, Blue Bird, Cadbury cocoa
skuLines.notes: Doubles as a baking staple, so it turns faster than hot-chocolate mix. 50g pack is the affordable unit.

skuLines.examples: Jawai Badam Keshari, Everest Milk Masala, Amul badam milk mix, Gits
skuLines.notes: Warm badam milk is a winter staple in Punjabi/Himachali households and a natural fit for a Sikh institution's guest and festival occasions. Tiny pack, tiny freight, good margin.

skuLines.examples: Nestle Everyday, Amulya, Amul Spray, Sapan
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes when hill milk supply is disrupted (monsoon roads, winter)
skuLines.notes: In a hill township where fresh-milk supply is not guaranteed, this is what makes tea possible on a bad-road day. Thinnest margin in the category and still non-negotiable. Absorbs moisture badly - keep in the jar/tin format through monsoon.

skuLines.line: Dairy whitener / SMP bulk for canteens
skuLines.examples: Amulya 1kg, Nestle Everyday 1kg, SMP 5-25kg institutional
skuLines.notes: Pairs with the bulk-tea line for the two canteens and hostel messes. Buy on a contract, not on the retail shelf price.

skuLines.examples: Nestle Milkmaid, Milkmaid Mini, Amul Mithai Mate
skuLines.notes: Cross-sells with cocoa for winter baking as much as it goes into coffee. Tins are hill-transport-proof and keep 12+ months.

skuLines.examples: Sofit soya, Alt Co oat drink, almond drink, coffee creamer
skuLines.notes: Serves lactose-intolerant residents and the international-student cohort, and plant-based is the named growth trend inside malted/hot drinks. Tetra needs no chiller and keeps 6-9 months - low-risk to try with 1-2 SKUs.

skuLines.examples: Avanti sugar cubes, Dhampure sachets, private-label 5g sticks
skuLines.priceBand: Rs 65 per 126 cubes; Rs 100-250 per sachet box
skuLines.notes: Canteen, guest house, department pantries and any vending point need portion sugar. Sells with the premix lines, not with grocery sugar.

skuLines.line: Jaggery powder / gur shakkar for tea
skuLines.examples: Parry's Amrit, Organic Tattva, Paawak cubes, local HP gur
skuLines.notes: North Indian winter habit and the local-sourcing opportunity: HP/Punjab gur can be bought short-haul at a far better margin than any branded tea. Cakes in humidity - jars and cubes over loose powder in monsoon.

skuLines.examples: Sugar Free Gold & Natura pellets/powder, Sugar Free Green Stevia, Zevic
skuLines.notes: Sits with tea and coffee, not with grocery sugar - a diabetic resident buys it in the same trip as tea. Pellet dispensers travel and store perfectly; near-zero spoilage risk.

skuLines.examples: Dabur Honey, Patanjali Honey, local Himalayan/multiflora honey
skuLines.notes: Overlaps the spreads category but sells on the tea/kadha occasion here. Local Himachali honey is a credible short-haul, high-margin, local-story line alongside the national brands.

trends2026: Sachet-first single-serve is the category's growth engine: sachets are ~40% of India's instant-coffee pack mix and the primary trial vehicle in tier 2-3, with Rs 5-Rs 10 units doing the recruiting that jars cannot.
Premiumisation inside instant coffee is outpacing volume: freeze-dried is now ~66% of instant-coffee value and consumers are trading up from spray-dried jars to 'Gold'/roastery tiers.

Functional and ayurvedic infusions are the fastest-moving part of tea - herbal tea growing ~12.6% CAGR against ~3% for tea overall - and the SKUs that win are benefit-labelled (throat, gut, sleep, immunity) rather than generically 'herbal'.

Malted health drinks have fragmented from one family jar into life-stage SKUs - kids, women, mothers, diabetic, elderly - plus millet/ragi-fortified clean-label variants (Millet Horlicks) and zero-added-sugar versions.
Refill pouches are displacing jars: 750g/1kg refills are the growth pack and are cheaper per gram, so the jar is now a one-time purchase and the refill is the repeat.

Cold coffee and RTD have moved into the hot-beverage aisle - Nestle's Apr-2025 cold-coffee launches, bottled cold brew, and protein cold-coffee shakes (Epigamia, Yoga Bar) - giving tea/coffee brands a summer line.
Plant-based milks and creamers (oat, soy, almond) have crossed from health stores into mainstream grocery and are now sold as coffee accessories, driven by lactose intolerance and vegan demand.

D2C and q-commerce brands (Blue Tokai's $35M Series C, Sleepy Owl, Blue Tea, Bevzilla) are creating brand awareness in small towns that physical stores must answer - tier II/III cities are now 60%+ of e-commerce transactions in this category.
Protein is creeping into hot beverages: protein-fortified malt drinks and coffee mixes, and Rs 100-150 5-serve protein trial packs replacing the Rs 3,000 tub as the entry SKU.
adjacentServices: A manned hot chai and filter-coffee counter at the main store and Ary Lite (Rs 10-15 a cup) - the same 1kg of tea earns several times the packet margin, and it converts 7.2 bills/resident/month into daily footfall.

Tea and coffee vending machines placed free in departments, hostel common rooms, the university blocks and the dispensary, with ARY selling the premix and sugar-sachet refills - a razor-and-blade annuity on the premix lines.
Contracted bulk supply to the two canteens and hostel messes: 5-10kg institutional tea, 1-25kg dairy whitener/SMP, sugar sachets, jaggery - priced on landed cost, not retail.
Monthly standing order for married staff quarters (1kg tea + a malt-drink refill + dairy whitener) with delivery, so the household never has a reason to buy tea on a trip to town.
Gift hampers built on Kangra (HP GI) and Darjeeling tea for the Trust's visitors, donors, parents and Diwali/Gurpurab gifting - the only premium-priced, locally sourced story this category offers.
Grind-to-order whole-bean coffee for faculty and the ~200 international students, which is the only way to sell specialty beans without them going stale on shelf.
Winter flask/thermos and electric-kettle sales (Rs 400-1,000) plus a paid flask-refill service - the hardware that makes hostel-room tea bags and premix work at all.
A hostel-admission starter kit at term start: kettle, mug, and a strip each of tea bags, coffee sachets and malt-drink sachets - captures the new student before habits form.
Refill-pack swap at the counter (bring the empty jar, buy the pouch) to move buyers off jars onto the cheaper, higher-turn refill pack.
Pre-monsoon and pre-winter seasonal pre-books for kahwa, hot chocolate, kadha and gur, so the one-truck-a-week hill road is not the reason the season is missed.
